facts.writes: disk_write loops synchronous single-sector writes; recording_session save is synchronous

analysis.important: A successful sector below 500ms does not imply a complete file commit fits the audio backlog. Consecutive busy periods accumulate while queue cannot drain.
analysis.example: Three consecutive 400ms sector waits exceed 1024ms even though no individual SD timeout fires. This is a permitted software timing scenario, not observed card behaviour.
analysis.limit: Available save time is less than 1024ms when queue already contains data; encryption, FAT metadata, transfer and commit time share the same budget.

required_change: Measure and bound entire save transaction, then implement cooperative/asynchronous persistence or prove total worst-case save fits measured queue slack for exact card. Raising per-sector timeout or modestly enlarging queue alone does not establish continuous recording.
hardware_test: timestamp save begin/end and queue high-water
exercise nearly-full/fragmented card, repeated writes and temperature
verify sticky overrun produces explicit recording failure, never silent success

results: 800ms with four queued blocks explicitly overruns, high-water16
native_reproduction.conclusion: Existing fault propagation works; uninterrupted capture requirement remains unmet under these simulated stalls. Saved prefix accounting remains intact. No physical card timing claim.
